title: Memory Semiconductor Shortage — Tech Giants Sramble for Samsung & SK Hynix Chips
summary: Tech giants scrambled for Samsung and SK Hynix memory chips amid shortages
detailed: AI investment growth has caused a memory semiconductor shortage, driving tech giants to compete for supplies from Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
Tesla CEO Elon Musk attempted to secure long-term supply agreements and factory financing guarantees with Samsung, but faced high demand and counter-inquiries from Samsung Chairman Lee Jae-yong.
Procurement contracts are shifting toward binding long-term agreements lasting up to five years amid the supply crunch.
Representatives from major tech and automotive companies, including Karma Automotive CEO Marques McCammon, have stationed staff or traveled repeatedly to South Korea to monitor supply conditions.
sentences: The explosive growth of artificial intelligence investments has triggered a severe memory semiconductor shortage, prompting global tech giants to fiercely compete for chip supplies from major South Korean manufacturers like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
Recent reports reveal that even Tesla CEO Elon Musk faced hurdles after attempting to secure long-term contracts and factory financing guarantees.
According to the Wall Street Journal, Capital Group portfolio manager Cal Kawaja shared details of a conversation with Musk at a June conference.
Musk reportedly proposed a long-term supply agreement with Samsung Electronics to resolve Tesla’s chip procurement challenges.
However, Samsung Chairman Lee Jae-yong countered by asking what additional incentives Musk could offer, noting that other companies were making similar proposals.
When Musk offered financial guarantees for Samsung’s new semiconductor plant construction project, Chairman Lee reportedly responded with the same question, emphasizing the high demand.

Industry analysts note that procurement contracts are rapidly evolving due to the ongoing supply crunch, with both suppliers and customers pushing for binding long-term agreements lasting up to five years.
To secure critical memory supplies, some large AI and tech enterprises have resorted to placing staff directly in South Korea.

Industry executives disclosed that representatives from major tech firms have set up accommodations right outside Samsung’s semiconductor plants, monitoring daily supply conditions and delivery schedules.
Meanwhile, automotive companies are intensifying their diplomatic efforts in Seoul.

Karma Automotive CEO Marques McCammon has visited South Korea four times over the past six months to meet with semiconductor suppliers, highlighting the extreme measures companies are taking during this generational supply crisis.
